description: Conformance corpus for the deprecation channel. Every runtime constructs a runtime from each case's `manifest`, supplying a host function for every path in `provided`, with a deprecation handler that records each notice it receives. The recorded notices must equal `expect` exactly, in order, with every field compared as a string.
notes: A notice is exactly `{ code, message, replacement }`. JS and Node pass the host's `onDeprecation` option a plain object; Rust passes `on_deprecation` a `Deprecation`; C# passes `OnDeprecation` a `Deprecation` record. The harness compares those three fields.

A code is raised at most once per runtime, whether or not a handler is set. `runtimes`, when present, constructs that many runtimes from the same host in turn; each one must raise `expect` on its own.

`binding-shadows-builtin` fires at construction when a top-level host binding is replaced by the runtime's own global of the same name. It names every replaced binding in one notice, in the fixed order events, hooks, xript. A binding named `console` wins over the runtime's console, so it raises nothing. Whether `events` and `xript` are replaced differs by runtime in some host shapes (see `spec/bindings.md`, Built-in Globals), so the cases here use only shapes where every runtime replaces the binding: `events` with events declared, and `hooks` supplied as a function.
`unbudgeted-handler` is raised only by runtimes that run hook and event handlers without a budget by default (JS and Node); each pins it in its own tests. See `spec/deprecations.md`.

cases.name: a host binding named events that the built-in replaces raises binding-shadows-builtin once

events.description: A host binding the runtime's events global replaces.

expect.message: host bindings replaced by a built-in global of the same name, which mods see instead: events
expect.replacement: Rename the binding or move it under a namespace.

cases.name: a host function named hooks raises binding-shadows-builtin
